subject: biology
title: Coronary heart disease and its treatments
key_idea: In coronary heart disease, fatty material builds up in the coronary arteries and narrows them. Less blood reaches the heart muscle, so it gets less oxygen. Treatments include drugs, surgery, replacement parts and lifestyle changes. Each has benefits and risks.

blocks.text: The coronary arteries supply the heart muscle with blood. This section covers what happens when they become blocked.

items.meaning: A disease where layers of fatty material build up inside the coronary arteries and narrow them.
A fatty substance in the blood. High levels add to the fatty material in the arteries.

diagram.alt: Put the steps from fatty deposits to chest pain or a heart attack in order.
steps: Layers of fatty material build up inside the coronary arteries
Less blood flows to the heart muscle
The heart muscle gets less oxygen and glucose
Less aerobic respiration, so less energy is released
Chest pain, tiredness, or a heart attack if the cells die

items: With less oxygen, more anaerobic respiration happens and lactic acid is made. This can cause muscle fatigue or chest pain.
A heart attack happens when the heart muscle cells do not get enough oxygen and die.
Fatty material narrows the coronary arteries and reduces blood flow to the heart muscle.
Less oxygen and glucose means less aerobic respiration and less energy.
Heart muscle cells die if they get too little oxygen.

blocks.text: Treatments fall into three groups: drugs, surgery or mechanical devices, and lifestyle changes. Exam questions ask you to weigh up the benefits and risks.

rows: Statins (drug)
Reduce blood cholesterol, which slows the build-up of fatty material.
Easy to take, not invasive and low cost.
Possible side effects such as muscle pain. Take time to work and must be taken long term.
Stent
A tube that holds a blocked coronary artery open.
Blood flow to the heart muscle increases straight away. Recovery is rapid.
Risk of infection, bleeding or a blood clot from the operation.
Bypass surgery
A section of blood vessel is used to go round a narrowed or blocked artery.
Restores blood flow to the heart muscle.
Major surgery, with the risks of an operation.
Valve replacement
A faulty valve is replaced with a biological or mechanical valve.
Valve opens fully or no longer leaks.
Risks of surgery.
Transplant or artificial heart
A donor heart (or heart and lungs) replaces a failing heart. An artificial heart keeps a patient alive while waiting, or lets the heart rest.
Can save the life of a patient with heart failure.
Risks of surgery. A donor organ must be found.

items: A healthier diet, with less fat and salt and more fruit and vegetables.
These lower the risk without surgery or drugs, but need long-term effort.
Statins slow the build-up of fatty material. Stents hold the artery open.
Faulty valves can be replaced, and a failing heart can be transplanted.
Always give a benefit and a risk when asked to evaluate.

checks.q: Explain the effect of a partly blocked coronary artery on the heart.
checks.a: Blood flow to the heart muscle is reduced, so less oxygen and glucose reach it. There is less aerobic respiration and less energy released, so the heart contracts less well.

checks.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of taking statins.
checks.a: Advantage: avoids an operation (or lowers cholesterol). Disadvantage: there could be side effects, or it must be taken on a regular basis.

checks.q: Describe how a stent treats coronary heart disease.
checks.a: It holds the blocked coronary artery open, so blood flow to the heart muscle cells increases.

exam_phrases: reduced blood / oxygen / glucose to the heart (muscle / tissue / cells)

mistakes.wrong: A blocked artery means the heart gets no blood.
mistakes.right: Say reduced blood flow, so less oxygen and glucose reach the heart muscle. Then link this to less respiration and less energy.

mistakes.wrong: Statins and stents are both better because they treat heart disease.
mistakes.right: Evaluate both. For top marks give advantages and disadvantages of each treatment, then a judgement.

mistakes.wrong: Statins remove fat from the arteries.
mistakes.right: Say statins decrease blood cholesterol and slow down the build-up of fatty material in the arteries.

worked_example.question: A heart attack is caused when the heart muscle cells do not get enough oxygen, causing the cells to die. Statins and stents are two treatments used to reduce the risk of someone having a heart attack. Evaluate the use of statins compared with the use of a stent to reduce the risk of a heart attack.
answer_points: Statins: easy to take, not invasive and lower cost than a stent operation.
Statins decrease blood cholesterol and slow down the build-up of fatty materials, which maintains blood flow to the heart muscle cells.
Statins: may have side effects such as muscle pain, take time to work and must be taken long term (or the patient might forget).
Stent: holds the blocked artery open, so blood flow to the heart muscle cells increases straight away. It stays in place for a long time and recovery is rapid.
Stent: risk of infection from the operation, risk of surgery such as bleeding, and a risk of a blood clot.
A judgement, supported by the reasons above.
worked_example.tip: For the top level you need arguments for and against both treatments, then a judgement.

exam_phrases: surgery to treat narrow or blocked arteries
lifestyle changes including healthy diet / more exercise

mistakes.right: Name all three groups: surgery (such as stents or bypass), lifestyle changes, and life-long medication.
Give an example: a healthy diet, more exercise or stopping smoking.

worked_example.question: Obesity can also cause cardiovascular disease to develop. Describe the different treatments available for cardiovascular disease.
answer_points: Surgery to treat narrow or blocked arteries, such as bypass surgery or stents.
Lifestyle changes, including a healthy diet or more exercise.
(Life-long) medication to prevent blood clots, reduce blood pressure or thin the blood.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each type of treatment: surgery, lifestyle and medication.

exam_phrases: fat blocking the blood vessels that supply the heart muscle
not enough glucose or oxygen for respiration
could be side effects of the drug
must take it on a regular basis

mistakes.wrong: A disadvantage of statins is that they are not a cure.
mistakes.right: Give a clear disadvantage: there could be side effects (such as liver damage or an upset stomach), or it must be taken on a regular basis, so a person may forget.

mistakes.wrong: Heart disease is caused by cholesterol blocking the veins.
mistakes.right: Fat blocks the blood vessels (the coronary arteries) that supply the heart muscle. The muscle then lacks glucose and oxygen for respiration.

worked_example.question: Taking a drug called statins is a treatment for CHD. The drug is taken every day and lowers the level of cholesterol in a person's blood. Suggest one advantage and one disadvantage of taking statins.
answer_points: Disadvantage: there could be side effects of the drug, or it must be taken on a regular basis.
worked_example.tip: A named side effect such as liver damage or an upset stomach is accepted. So is forgetting to take the drug.
